reason: Confirmed by driving, not by reading. Chromium at 1440x960, ?v=light&state=<state>, reduced-motion settled, aria snapshot of .kpis. Full state returns exactly the three names the seat quotes: link "3 haven’t moved in a fortnight 3 jobs haven’t moved in a fortnight, of 9 jobs open", link "2 past the day they were due 2 jobs past the day they were due, of 9 jobs open", link "1 has nobody’s name on it 1 job has nobody’s name on it, of 9 jobs open". Partial keeps two such links (the overdue card degrades to a div), first-run one. The code reading is right at lately.html:675-694: kpi()'s body aria-hides only .glyph and .meter, so .t-num and .t-small are live tree content and a link takes its name from the concatenation of its contents. The numbers in the fix are right against the real source — .t-num, .t-small and the unavailable branch's "Not available" .t-label are precisely and exhaustively the three unhidden visible spans in body, and the .sr span is their sibling, not their child, so hiding them cannot bury it. The non-link cards (n===0, unavailable) are divs and take no accessible name, but a browse-mode reader still walks their text in order and hears the same doubling, so applying the fix to both branches as proposed is the right sweep, not overreach. Not already handled and not a gate restatement: interaction-check.mjs:116 asserts only that a name EXISTS, and :166 only that no .sr sits under aria-hidden — both of which the doubled name satisfies. The surface already proves the opposite for the chart at :1061-1088 ("the chart is announced once", leaves === 1), which is the same class fixed in r1 on a different element and never swept to the KPI row; this is that class surviving, not a re-raise of chart-is-announced-twice. Severity is correctly classed: nothing untrue is asserted and the count is still reachable, so this is not misleading or blocking; it is not taste either, because the authored sentence exists specifically so the row is not heard as loose numerals and it is prefixed by exactly those loose numerals. Defect stands. The lead card is correctly exempted — its .sr ("Every card in this row is counted out of these 9 open jobs.") states the shared-denominator contract rather than repeating its visible text.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix as proposed — aria-hidden="true" on the .t-num span in both branches, on the .t-small phrase span, and on the unavailable branch's "Not available" .t-label — leaving .sr as the sole tree content of kpi()'s body, which is exactly the shape the chart already ships. Add one thing the seat omits, or the class returns on the next template edit the way it returned here after r1 fixed it on the chart: mirror the chart's assertion for the row in interaction-check.mjs — walk each .kpi:not(.lead) skipping aria-hidden subtrees and assert exactly one text leaf, that it is the .sr, and that the .sr is non-empty, across full, partial and first-run. The existing chart walker at :1066-1080 is directly reusable. Leave leadKpi() alone and leave the skeleton alone — the sk-wrap is already aria-hidden at :974 and has its .sr stripped at :1144.
breaks: Nothing in either gate: interaction-check.mjs:116 derives its name from el.textContent, which ignores aria-hidden, so the named-element assertion still passes; :199, :215, :288-297, :311-313, :804 and :950-954 all read textContent or query the DOM, none of which aria-hidden touches; audit.mjs measures palette, weight, contrast and geometry and never reads the tree. Re-measure two things after it lands. First, WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name: today the visible string is contained in the name; after the fix the name reads "3 jobs haven’t moved…" against a visible "3" plus "haven’t moved in a fortnight", so the numeral and its noun no longer line up for a voice-control user. The phrase itself survives verbatim as a contiguous substring, which is what speech targeting actually matches on, so this is acceptable — but confirm the phrase stays verbatim in the .sr if the copy is ever reworded, or the link becomes unspeakable. Second, run the full seven states plus 390/768/1280/1440: after the fix every card's entire visible content is aria-hidden and its entire accessible content is visually hidden, so any future card variant that forgets its .sr line goes completely silent instead of degrading to a loose numeral — which is precisely what the added assertion above is there to catch.
